item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
872
ABNT20 KNHC 191149
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM EDT Sat Sep 19 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Eastern Subtropical Atlantic (AL99):
Showers and thunderstorms have become more concentrated near the
center of a low pressure system located several hundred miles
southwest of the western Azores since yesterday. A short-lived
tropical depression or tropical storm is expected to form later
today or tonight while moving north-northeastward at about 5 mph,
but remaining well to the southwest of the Azores. Upper-level winds
are forecast to become less conducive for development beginning
late Sunday.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Berg

item.title: Tropical Depression Six Public Advisory Number 1
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM GMT Sat Sep 19 2026 
886 
WTNT31 KNHC 191448
TCPAT1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Six Advisory Number   1
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
300 PM GMT Sat Sep 19 2026
 
...NEW TROPICAL DEPRESSION FORMS SOUTHWEST OF THE AZORES...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 PM GMT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...32.6N 33.6W
ABOUT 525 MI...845 KM SW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...N OR 360 DEGREES AT 2 MPH...4 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1009 MB...29.80 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 PM GMT (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Six was
located near latitude 32.6 North, longitude 33.6 West. The
depression is moving toward the north near 2 mph (4 km/h). This
system is expected to generally move to the northeast for the next 
24 to 36 hours, before turning toward the southwest in a couple of 
days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Slight strengthening is possible during the next 24 hours, however 
after that gradual weakening is expected to occur. 
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1009 mb (29.80 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 PM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Berg

item.title: Tropical Depression Six Forecast Discussion Number 1
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM GMT Sat Sep 19 2026 
000
WTNT41 KNHC 191449
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Depression Six Discussion Number   1
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
300 PM GMT Sat Sep 19 2026
 
A recent ASCAT pass showed that the system NHC has been monitoring 
southwest of the Azores (AL99) has a well-defined circulation and 
peak wind vectors were around 26 kt. The stucture of the cyclone 
still has the bulk of the convection on the northern side, and that 
area of convection has persisted for more than 12 hours. However, 
the cyclone appears to lie along the northern edge of a zone of 
strong westerly shear. In addition the most recent TAFB 
Dvorak fix was T2.0/30 kt, which has persisted since the last 
forecast cycle. Based on the given data, this system has been 
started as Tropical Depression Six with an initial intensity of 30 
kt.

Tropical Depression Six is currently meandering, however it should 
start to increase in speed and move generally to the northeast for 
the next 36 h as a trough to the north weakens the ridge to the 
northeast. Around 48 h, the ridge is expected to build back, which 
will force the cyclone to move towards the southwest. The system is 
expected to remain on this heading for the rest of the forecast 
period. The current NHC track forecast is in good agreement with the 
HCCA and GDMI.

The depression is expected to move into a slightly more favorable 
environment, between two areas of intense shear. This could allow 
for some slight intensification to occur for the next day or so. 
After 36 h, the system is expected to move into an area of higher 
shear as the previously mentioned trough starts to negatively impact 
the cyclone, thus resulting in gradual weakening. The system is 
expected to become a post-tropical remnant low around 72 h, and then 
dissipate around 120 h. However, the guidance from the GFS and ECMWF 
show significant differences in when dissipation occurs. The GFS has 
the cyclone dissipating much sooner around 72 h, while the ECMWF has 
dissipation occuring around 120 h. The current NHC intensity 
forecast is in the middle of the guidance envelope and is slightly 
under HCCA.
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
